summary: A reef light at Lloyd Harbor's mouth: an 1857 brick light lost to fire in 1947, the 1912 concrete tower that replaced it, its keepers, and the Society that runs it.

structures.note: Lloyd's Harbor light; station destroyed by fire 12 Nov 1947 (USLHS); LighthouseFriends says the dwelling was destroyed
Two-story dwelling on a brick foundation; destroyed by fire 12 Nov 1947
Cast reinforced concrete; 34 ft base to lantern centre per USLHS; the Society gives 42 ft
One-story cast concrete keeper's quarters, attached to the tower

access.note: Reached only by boat on tours run by the Huntington Lighthouse Preservation Society from the Goldstar Battalion Beach dock; not handicap accessible; children under five not admitted.

visit.note: Tower climbed on Society tours only.

facts.agency: Huntington Lighthouse Preservation Society, Inc. (nonprofit; the Department of the Interior announced its 2011 transfer to the Society)

events.note: Lloyd's Harbor light: two-story wooden dwelling on a brick foundation, square brick tower attached at one corner
First lit 15 November 1857
Fifth-order Henry-Lepaute Fresnel, fixed white, focal plane 48 ft
Gale of 22 November 1870; repaired, and a granite wall built (Board's 1871 report as quoted by LighthouseFriends)
Congress appropriates $2,000 for stones placed around the station, after ice damage to the sea wall in 1872
Contract to take down part of the east breakwater and build a new one to protect the foundations of the dwelling and tower
Underpinning of the dwelling's southwest corner rebuilt; minor repairs
Congress appropriates $40,000 for a new offshore light (4 March per LighthouseFriends; 7 March per the Society)
Cast reinforced concrete tower on a concrete caisson, sunk offshore
Light passed from the old tower to the new on 16 June 1912
Keeper Marvin E. Burnham rescues a man and a woman from a leaking schooner in Huntington Bay (LighthouseFriends only)
Keeper E. J. Brunner rescues two men who fell overboard from a motorboat, 21 September

Old dwelling and station destroyed by fire 12 November 1947 after a fire started in the fireplace by hunters

corrections.current: tower, concrete, concrete, built 1857, 13.0 m, standing
corrections.proposed: tower, cast reinforced concrete, built 1912, standing; the 1857 brick light on Lloyd's Neck was lost in the 1947 fire
corrections.why: The standing tower dates from 1912 (USLHS Year Tower Established 1912; LighthouseFriends). The 1857 light was brick, and its Lloyd's Harbor station is recorded as destroyed by fire on 12 November 1947 (USLHS).
USLHS gives the height of the light above mean high water as 37 feet (about 11.3 m). Check against the USCG Light List before adopting.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record gives 1857 and 1912 because it holds two lights on one station: the 1857 brick light (first lit 15 November 1857) and the 1912 concrete tower (light passed to it 16 June 1912). Both are recorded here.

notes_for_editor:
Sources. The NRHP nomination (NRIS 89000501) is a 22 KB 'not yet digitized' placeholder; the story uses only the NPGallery metadata (architects, listing date). Chronicling America searches for Lloyd Harbor lighthouse, 1907-1912 and 1912-1919, returned nothing relevant (the hits were unrelated pages), so no newspaper is cited. Wikipedia was read for leads only and is not cited. The 1857 light's keepers and the 1912 tower's construction rest on LighthouseFriends and the USLHS; the local corpus has no Board reports from 1857-1890 or 1900-1912.

Disagreements left open in the text: LighthouseFriends gives 4 March 1907 for the appropriation and the Society gives 7 March 1907; LighthouseFriends calls the tower the oldest reinforced-concrete lighthouse on the East Coast, while the Society's 2026 announcement calls it the only concrete lighthouse on the coast; the NRHP listing is 1988 (LighthouseFriends) or 31 May 1989 (NPGallery); the tower height is 34 ft to lantern (USLHS), 42 ft (Society); the lens of 1912 (fourth order per LighthouseFriends; fifth-order original per USLHS); McGlone's time at Lloyd Harbor is 24 years (LighthouseFriends) or 1885-1912 (roster).

Not verified: the record's characteristic (Iso W 6s) and range (9 nm) are not confirmed by any source read; no Light List was consulted, so neither appears in facts. Automation: LighthouseFriends gives 1948; Wikipedia's 1949 is not cited. Isabelle McGlone's quotation is LighthouseFriends quoting her recollection by name; it is second-hand, via LighthouseFriends. The 1920 and 1929 speedboat rescues rest on LighthouseFriends alone; the 1929 motorboat rescue and the 1930 rescue are in the Bulletin.

People. Only Robert McGlone's two stints are one person across two towers. Harrigan is a household helper, not a keeper, and is not on the roster. Roster lines follow the archive's spelling; 'person' is set on every archive line because each is that archive record's stint. The 1943 Bentley line sits between White's two stints as printed by the archive.

Location. The record's position (40.910726, -73.43128) matches LighthouseFriends (40.91069, -73.4313). The USLHS Huntington Harbor place gives 40 deg 54.4 min N, 73 deg 25.5 min W, about 0.7 km away; the USLHS point is not used.

Access. Nothing here encourages a landing or a climb outside the Society's tours. The 2026 tour season is over; 2027 dates were not posted when checked on 2026-10-22.
